concepts.label: Absolute URI
concepts.definition: A URI that already has a scheme. A reference without one is rejected, and RFC 3986 relative-reference resolution is not this package's job.

code_evidence.quote: `urisolver` resolves **absolute URIs** into usable resources.

concepts.label: Scheme dispatch
concepts.definition: The core checks scheme grammar, compares schemes case-insensitively, and hands the original URI to the resolver registered for that scheme.

code_evidence.quote: The core validates syntax before dispatch.
Split an absolute URI into scheme / scheme-specific-part / fragment.

concepts.label: URI fragment
concepts.definition: The fragment is split off before dispatch and is never an identifier. Resolvers must not turn it into a path, a key, or a selection.

code_evidence.quote: The fragment is not scheme-specific and a scheme definition cannot redefine it (RFC 7595 §3; RFC 3986 §3.5).
Carry a request fragment onto a namespace target.

references.note: bibliographic pointer; no sentence was fetched

concepts.label: Opaque payload
concepts.definition: When a resolver marks its payload opaque, logs, errors, reprs, and temporary paths show the scheme plus a digest, not the payload.

code_evidence.quote: The scheme may always appear in the clear (it is needed to diagnose `UnknownSchemeError`).
URI and message redaction (§4.1, §24.1).

concepts.label: Redaction
concepts.definition: Secrets, credential-bearing backend errors, and opaque URI payloads are stripped before they are logged or chained onto an exception.

code_evidence.quote: Backend exceptions frequently carry URLs with embedded credentials.
URI and message redaction (§4.1, §24.1).

concepts.label: Scheme naming
concepts.definition: A private scheme uses a reversed domain the deployer controls. A short unregistered name is not a conforming choice.

code_evidence.quote: Scheme names occupy a single global namespace.

references.page_title: Guidelines and Registration Procedures for URI Schemes

concepts.label: URI equivalence
concepts.definition: The core case-folds the scheme and does not otherwise normalize. Percent-encoding, dot segments, and default ports stay the resolver's problem.

code_evidence.quote: `urisolver` does not implement RFC 3986 §6 normalisation.
Return *uri* with only its scheme case-normalised (RFC 3986 §6.2.2.1).

concepts.definition: Every scheme a deployment registers needs a page in SCHEMES.md stating syntax, operations, and security before the scheme is usable.

code_evidence.quote: RFC 7595 §3.3 and §3.4 require a scheme definition to state how the scheme is expected to function: how a URI of the scheme maps into an identifier or protocol action, what operations are...
Deployment-specific schemes follow the template below and get a page in this file before they are registered.

concepts.label: Public resolve API
concepts.definition: Context.resolve is the real entry point. The module-level resolve function is a process-default convenience that library code should not rely on.

code_evidence.quote: The context is primary; the module-level function is sugar.
Resolve *uri*.

concepts.label: Resolve context
concepts.definition: The context owns resolver lifetime, the secrets provider, the memory limit, and session reuse. Closing it invalidates resources it produced.

code_evidence.quote: `ResolveContext` is a context manager.
ResolveContext — session ownership (§5, §23).

concepts.label: Resolved resource
concepts.definition: The object a resolver returns. It keeps the caller's URI and the concrete URI, and it is bound to the context that created it.

code_evidence.quote: A `ResolvedResource` may hold an open session.
Protocol definitions (§6, §14, §17).

concepts.label: Resource info
concepts.definition: A cheap description filled in at resolve time: kind, existence, and optional size or shape. It must not pull the bulk bytes.

code_evidence.quote: Cheap, best-effort description obtained during or shortly after resolution.
ResourceInfo and Kind (§7).

concepts.label: Tier 0 baseline
concepts.definition: info and materialize are present on every resource. Policy may make them fail, but it may not hide them.

code_evidence.quote: Tier 0 operations are **universally present**.

concepts.label: Materialize
concepts.definition: Delivery of a resource into a file or memory destination. Resolve itself does not download or convert; this call does.

code_evidence.quote: Tier 0 operations are **universally present**.
MaterializedResult (§10).

concepts.label: Canonical media type
concepts.definition: The resolver names the byte encoding for a structured resource. The core does not invent one.

code_evidence.quote: A byte-level representation of a structured resource requires choosing a serialization, and the core must not choose one on the resolver's behalf — that would be exactly the invented semantics §3...

concepts.label: Form
concepts.definition: What the caller wants back from memory delivery: a backend-native object, bytes, or an optional array or table.

code_evidence.quote: A form is *what the caller wants back*, independent of protocol.
Destinations and forms (§9–§12).

concepts.label: Materialized result
concepts.definition: The value plus enough URI and strategy metadata for an outside provenance layer to record what was staged.

code_evidence.quote: `__repr__` must use redacted URIs (§4.1) and must never include `value` for memory results.
MaterializedResult (§10).

concepts.label: Materialization strategy
concepts.definition: A short token on the result that says whether the backend did the work, the bytes were sliced locally, or a reference was returned.

code_evidence.quote: `"read-then-select"` must also append a human-readable entry to `warnings`.

concepts.label: Strict efficiency
concepts.definition: When the context flag is set, a delivery that would read the whole object and slice it locally is refused before the transfer starts.

code_evidence.quote: `"read-then-select"` must also append a human-readable entry to `warnings`.

concepts.label: File destination
concepts.definition: A caller-chosen path. Successful delivery leaves that path in place, written via a temporary name and an atomic replace.

code_evidence.quote: Failure cleanup removes the temporary artefact only.
Destinations and forms (§9–§12).

concepts.label: Reference policy
concepts.definition: Copy is the default. A link or in-place path is returned only when the caller asked, and failure cleanup must not delete that source.

code_evidence.quote: Failure cleanup removes the temporary artefact only.

concepts.label: Memory destination
concepts.definition: An in-memory delivery in a chosen form, bounded by the destination or context byte limit.

code_evidence.quote: The context supplies a default `max_bytes`; `Context(memory_limit=None)` disables it.
Destinations and forms (§9–§12).

concepts.label: Selection
concepts.definition: The only portable subsetting in the baseline is numpy basic indexing, plus a column list for tables. Anything else is not a core query language.

code_evidence.quote: Selection is portable at Tier 0 for one narrow, already-standard case.
Selection types (§13).

concepts.label: Native selection
concepts.definition: A wrapper that passes a backend-specific query through untouched. Using it means the caller has accepted protocol coupling.

code_evidence.quote: Selection is portable at Tier 0 for one narrow, already-standard case.
Opaque pass-through wrapper declaring protocol coupling (§13).

concepts.label: Tier 1 facet
concepts.definition: An optional declared interface borrowed from an existing library, so generic code can do more than fetch the whole object.

code_evidence.quote: A facet is a small, optional, *declared* protocol.
Protocol definitions (§6, §14, §17).

concepts.label: Stream facet
concepts.definition: A binary reader for resources that can be opened as a byte stream, including range reads where the backend supports them.

code_evidence.quote: A facet is a small, optional, *declared* protocol.
Protocol definitions (§6, §14, §17).

concepts.label: Array facet
concepts.definition: Shape, dtype, and numpy basic indexing on an array resource. Fancy indexing is not part of the facet.

code_evidence.quote: Numpy basic indexing only.
Protocol definitions (§6, §14, §17).

concepts.label: Table facet
concepts.definition: Column names and an optional row count, with a read that can ask for a subset of columns.

code_evidence.quote: A facet is a small, optional, *declared* protocol.
Protocol definitions (§6, §14, §17).

concepts.label: Container facet
concepts.definition: Named children of a container, each itself a resolved resource. Keys are single path segments, not a path traversal API.

code_evidence.quote: Container keys are validated as single path segments: empty, `.`, `..`, absolute paths, and keys containing a separator or NUL are rejected with `KeyError`.
Protocol definitions (§6, §14, §17).

concepts.label: Tier 2 native pass-through
concepts.definition: Backend operations the wrapper does not rename or reinterpret. Callers who use them accept that the call is protocol-specific.

code_evidence.quote: For everything else, the resolver exposes the protocol's own operations:

concepts.label: Capability
concepts.definition: supports is the one answer for what a resource can do. capabilities and attribute lookup report that same set.

code_evidence.quote: `supports(name)` is authoritative.

concepts.label: Policy filtering
concepts.definition: A resolver may hide backend operations. That filter is a convenience in this process, not a security boundary.

code_evidence.quote: In-process Python filtering cannot be enforcement: the caller shares the address space with the session object, the transport, and the credentials.

concepts.label: Resolver
concepts.definition: The plugin that interprets one scheme: sessions, credentials, info, and materialize. The core does not parse the scheme-specific part for it.

code_evidence.quote: The resolver owns:
Protocol definitions (§6, §14, §17).

concepts.label: Registry
concepts.definition: The map from scheme to resolver. Two schemes may share a protocol and still point at different servers and credentials.

code_evidence.quote: Two schemes may use the same protocol with entirely independent servers, credentials, routing, policy, URI syntax and configuration.
Scheme → resolver registry (§18).

concepts.label: Resolver plugin
concepts.definition: An installed distribution registers schemes through entry points. Those points are listed at import and imported on first use.

code_evidence.quote: Installing a package must be sufficient to make a scheme resolvable.
Entry-point plugin discovery (§19).

concepts.label: Namespace indirection
concepts.definition: A namespace URI asks which concrete URI an identifier maps to for this caller right now. That is not RFC 3986 reference resolution.

code_evidence.quote: *What concrete URI does this identifier resolve to, for this caller, right now?*
Namespace types and cache (§20).

concepts.label: Namespace service
concepts.definition: A self-hosted POST /resolve endpoint. The process is urisolver's; the routing function is the deployer's.

code_evidence.quote: The server infrastructure is `urisolver`'s.
Self-hosted namespace service (§21).
CLI: urisolver serve (§21).

concepts.label: Bespoke routing
concepts.definition: Persistent names stay small because the private routing rules live in the deployer's resolver, not in the core.

code_evidence.quote: The user-supplied router may contain private and security-sensitive logic: consult private databases, contact internal APIs, decrypt opaque tokens via OpenBao Transit / AWS KMS / Google Cloud KMS...

concepts.label: Secrets provider
concepts.definition: A get_secret lookup by id. The core never stores the values, and the resolver asks only for the id the catalog selected.

code_evidence.quote: The provider knows the infrastructure.
SecretsProvider protocol (§24).

concepts.label: Error model
concepts.definition: Failures are typed by stage: bad URI, unknown scheme, access, namespace, materialize, selection, secrets, and plugins.

code_evidence.quote: `AccessError` is deliberately not under `ResolutionError`: entitlement is decided at call time, not at resolution time (§16.1), so a resource may resolve cleanly and then raise...
Base error for all urisolver failures.

concepts.label: Async names
concepts.definition: aresolve and amaterialize are reserved so later async support does not fork the API. Sync callers do not need an event loop.

code_evidence.quote: Resolvers **may** implement them; `supports("aresolve")` reports whether they do.
Reserved async resolve name (§26).

concepts.label: file scheme
concepts.definition: The built-in resolver for local paths: stat for info, a stream facet, and byte contents for memory delivery.

code_evidence.quote: Kind FILE (or CONTAINER for a directory) info() stat-derived: exists, size_bytes, media_type by extension facets stream (always), array/table only via optional codecs Tier 2 open(), stat()...
file: resolver (§27.1).

concepts.label: Tiled resolver
concepts.definition: An optional resolver that reads a Tiled node. The server address and the secret id come from the local resolution catalog.

code_evidence.quote: Independently configured schemes: `gov.bnl.nsls2.tiled:`, `gov.bnl.nsls2.tiled-ssrl:`.
Tiled resolver (§27.2).
Tiled server named by the local resolution catalog.

concepts.label: Globus resolver
concepts.definition: An optional Transfer resolver for one collection path. File delivery is a copy; memory delivery stages through the catalog's staging collection.

code_evidence.quote: `GlobusResolver` (extra `[globus]`) is one path on a Transfer collection.
`com.urisolver.example.globus` — reverse-DNS private use (RFC 7595 §3.8).
Globus Transfer resolver.
Globus collection named by the local resolution catalog.

concepts.label: Resolution catalog
concepts.definition: A local YAML file that binds a scheme to a server, a secret id, and optional path-prefix overrides. Secret values are not in the file.

code_evidence.quote: Deployment-specific schemes follow the template below and get a page in this file before they are registered.
Local resolution catalog shared by the example schemes.
Pick a secret id for one resource path.

concepts.label: Conformance baseline
concepts.definition: A resolver-agnostic test suite shipped with the package. A plugin that does not pass it is not a conforming resolver.

code_evidence.quote: The suite is shipped as `urisolver.testing.baseline` so third-party resolvers can import and run it.
Baseline conformance suite (§31) — matches installed API.
